source: Quiz 5 - Sessions 1-6: Model Training, Alignment, and the Agent Harness
question: How can two post-training procedures differ even when both use human preferences?

options.text: A preferred output is a demonstration, so comparisons cannot guide learning
options.feedback: Comparisons can identify a preferred output without supplying the same training information as a demonstration. The notes explicitly include preferences as a learning source.

options.text: Preferences can guide training through several different methods
options.feedback: The notes identify alternatives to the classic reinforcement-learning pipeline. The common role of preference information does not make the procedures identical.

options.text: Preference information describes inference rather than further model training
options.feedback: Preferences can supply learning information during post-training. Their use is not limited to the current inference response.

options.text: Every preference method requires humans to write a target for each next token
options.feedback: That requirement confuses different learning signals. The notes distinguish text-derived next-token targets, demonstrations, and comparisons of outputs.
